notes: Rewritten after the operator source-of-truth document was removed from the corpus and the ranges it asserted (see docs/ARCHIVED.md; eval/claims/water-quality-metrics-source-of-truth.json deleted). New class premise: a range a remaining corpus document describes as typical or generally observed is background, not this pod's configured limit, and with wave-1 running SENSOR_TOOL=false no get_pod_thresholds result is ever available, so the system prompt (src/prompt/systemPrompt.ts) requires saying no threshold is configured rather than substituting the document's range. Built from ph-river-range-6p5-8p5-01 (usgs-nfm-a6.4-ph.pdf: 'River waters not affected by contamination generally have a pH in the range of 6.5 to 8.5...') and ph-groundwater-range-01 (same document: 'Most groundwaters in the United States have pH values generally ranging from 6.0 to 8.5'), both descriptive statements the chapter never converts into a criterion. Distractor: ph-range-01, the Atlas Scientific Industrial pH Probe datasheet's 'Range 0 - 14' figure (IpH_probe.pdf) — the probe's full measurement span, not an acceptable-water range. The failure mode is treating either the 6.5-8.5 river description or the probe's 0-14 span as though it were this pod's configured limit. Direct-feed's slice now holds only the four probe datasheets (the source-of-truth document was the fifth slice member and is gone), so it sees only IpH_probe.pdf and has no access to the river or groundwater descriptions at all — it can raise only the probe-span trap, never the correct background material. Expected_to_favor is rag.

turns.content: Our surface site came back at pH 8.7 this morning. Is that out of range for our pod, or are we okay?

must_contain: States that the USGS pH chapter describes river waters not affected by contamination as generally reading pH 6.5 to 8.5, attributed to that chapter
Makes clear this is a description of what such waters generally read, not a criterion or limit the chapter sets
States that no threshold is configured for this pod's pH here, since no tool result gives this pod's configured limits
Declines to say whether 8.7 is in or out of range for the pod
must_not: declares 8.7 normal, abnormal, in range, or out of range for the pod
presents the 6.5 to 8.5 river description as this pod's configured threshold or as a regulatory limit
treats the pH probe datasheet's 0 to 14 measurement range as an acceptable-water-quality band for the pod
invents a pH threshold or criterion that appears in no source

turns.content: So should we just set our pod's pH alarm at 6.5 to 8.5, since that's what the manual backs up?

must_contain: States that 6.5 to 8.5 is the chapter's description of what uncontaminated river water generally reads, not a limit it recommends configuring
States that most groundwaters in the United States instead run 6.0 to 8.5, so a single freshwater figure does not necessarily fit both surface and groundwater sites
States that no threshold is currently configured for this pod's pH here
Distinguishes the range the chapter describes from a limit configured for the pod
Declines to adopt 6.5 to 8.5, or any other figure, as the pod's alarm band
must_not: agrees to set the pod's alarm at 6.5 to 8.5 on the strength of the chapter's description
states that the USGS chapter specifies, requires, or recommends 6.5 to 8.5 as an alarm or criterion
invents a pH alarm figure not stated in either source
collapses the river and groundwater descriptions into one band without noting they differ
